text:
emma: Quick live-thread after today's Q&A: a few teams asked for a short checklist for kernel-v3 canary monitoring and who to ping on anomalies. I'll start.

ryan: Thanks emma. Two quick bullets: 1) watch p95 token latency by model and seq-len buckets, 2) monitor quantization-variant error spikes (we've seen weird tokenization edge cases).

theo: Add: watch end-to-end prompt-set eval scores. We have a baseline shipper that posts diffs to the perf dashboard every 10m. Threshold is -1.0% relative quality.

priya: Practical ops: can someone confirm the flag names and where teams can opt in? I want to enable for our staging env.

marta: Flag names: runtime.kernel_v3.enabled (global), runtime.kernel_v3.kv_evict_policy (values: fixed_ttl, lru_weight), runtime.kernel_v3.batch_window_ms. Opt-in is via the Console > Deployments > Canary toggles or the env var for Private: REDWOOD_KERNEL_V3=1. Docs coming.

emma: Nice. Any change to default batching window? A couple folks worried about small-req latency.

ryan: Default stays 10ms. We built an adaptive micro-batcher but it's behind a feature flag. Experiments may flip to 12ms for some high-throughput SKUs, but only behind opt-in.

priya: What about cache eviction semantics? Will prefix/KV invalidation happen more often?

theo: No change to TTL default (60s). New lru_weight option evicts by cumulative token weight which helps long-context workloads. It's off by default in hosted canary.

marta: For Dedicated customers, we can enable lru_weight earlier if they request it; need a signed change request. Reach out to customer-sre.

emma: Rollout schedule? We said next sprint but want concrete dates for teams to plan.

ryan: Canary roll starts 1957030000 (UTC epoch) at 5% traffic, then 1957050000 ramp to 30% if metrics stable, final roll 1957100000. These are tentative but accurate enough for planning.

priya: Who owns automatic rollback on quality regressions? I want the contact list.

theo: Research pipelines own eval-based automatic pause. Infra automation will cut traffic if latency or error thresholds hit. Pager on-call: infra-oncall, escalation to ryan then theo. I'll add a page with contacts.

emma: Can we get a short list of dashboards/queries to check during canary (so SREs can add alerts quickly)?

marta: Sure: 1) perf.tokens.p95_by_model_seq, 2) perf.eval.delta_recent, 3) infra.kv.evictions_per_min, 4) infra.batch.window_ms_distribution. I'll post Grafana links in the canary runbook.

ops-bot: Canary job scheduled: kernel-v3-canary at 1957030000 (automated note) :spiral_calendar:

ryan: Office hours planned Friday 4pm PT — I'll demo the dashboard and go through rollback runbook. Link: https://intra.redwood/events/kernel-v3-office-hours

priya: One last ask from product: will customers see any billing changes?

theo: No immediate pricing change. If the kernel increases throughput in a way that lowers per-token cost we'll surface recommendations, but billing SKUs remain the same for now.

emma: Thanks all. I'll assemble the checklist and post it to #release-war-room and tag infra-oncall.

marta: Posted checklist -> https://intra.redwood/docs/kernel-v3-canary-checklist (will update with links).

emma: Great :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
